references.text: Prohibition against following the customs and practices of the nations, which parallels the warning against learning the detestable things of the peoples.
Warnings against the detestable practices of the Canaanites that caused the land to vomit them out, something Israel must avoid.
Prohibition against following the customs of the nations God is driving out, because they did all these things.
Warning against adopting the religious practices of the nations after God has destroyed them from the land.
The promise that God will give them the land and drive out the nations, with a command not to make covenants with them.
King Ahaz walked in the detestable practices of the nations, as an example of what Israel was warned against.
Israel followed the customs of the nations whom the Lord had driven out, in direct disobedience to this warning.
King Manasseh did according to the detestable practices of the nations that the Lord had driven out before Israel.
Ezekiel shows that Israel committed detestable acts that led God to withdraw from the sanctuary.
